title: Drinking Water and Food Hygiene on Safari
excerpt: Do not drink tap water in Tanzania. What to drink instead, how lodges handle food hygiene and how to avoid an upset stomach.
body:
Stomach trouble is the most common health complaint for travellers. A few simple habits help a lot.

## Water

- Do not drink tap water.
- Use bottled, filtered or boiled water, also for brushing your teeth.
- Many safari vehicles carry drinking water. Some lodges offer refill stations to reduce plastic.
- A reusable bottle with a filter is a good option.

## Ice

In good hotels and lodges, ice is usually made from treated water. At street stalls, it is better to skip it.

## Food

- Eat food that is freshly cooked and hot.
- Peel fruit yourself.
- Be careful with salads at simple places.
- Wash or disinfect your hands before eating.

## Lodges and camps

Most safari lodges and camps are used to international guests and handle hygiene carefully.

## If it happens

Drink plenty of fluids, use oral rehydration salts and rest. See a doctor if you have a high fever or symptoms last.

This is general information. See [staying healthy on safari](/blog/safari-health-tips/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
